Open Days & Tours
Open days for entry into Year R for September 2027 will take place on:
Friday 16th October @ 10.30am
Friday 13th November @ 10.30am
Friday 27th November @ 10.30am
There will be a limited number of places per day, so please do contact us on 01428 713216 or office@stjohns-farnham.surrey.sch.uk to make a booking.
If you would like to make a late application to join us this September, or to make an in-year transfer for any year group at any time, we would love to meet you. Please do contact us to make an appointment to come into school and meet Mrs Stevens for a tour, and to answer any questions you may have.
You can give the office a call on 01428 713216 to let us know your availability or email Mrs Batchelor in the school on office@stjohns-farnham.surrey.sch.uk
More information can be found on our dedicated in-Year applications page here

Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to St John’sA very warm welcome to our school and our website. We hope you find your visit both interesting and informative, giving you a real insight into life at St John’s. Please do explore our virtual tour, and if you would like to see the school in action, we would be delighted to welcome you for a visit.
Our Vision and ValuesAt St John's, we believe in a truly child‑centred education, where every pupil can access an exciting, rich, and varied curriculum. Through this approach, our children become increasingly independent, resilient, and confident learners who develop a genuine love of learning.
Our values underpin all that we do. Every child in our care is treasured as an individual so that they can let their light shine — our vision for each member of our school community.
Learning Beyond the ClassroomWe have a strong love for the great outdoors. All children enjoy weekly forest school sessions and have access to a trim trail. PE lessons take place on our sports field, and at school we offer climbing apparatus, beautiful playground equipment, and well‑resourced classrooms to enrich learning.
Our Staff TeamWe are proud of our exceptional team here at St John’s, and I am delighted to be a part of such a dedicated, caring, and inspiring community. Together, we strive to create a nurturing environment where every child can flourish.
Find Out MoreWe invite you to explore our website to learn more about our school, our staff, and our curriculum. If you would like to read the full Ofsted and SIAMS reports, you can click here.
If you have any questions, please get in touch - we are always happy to help.

National Arts Award
Budding young artists at St John’s Infant School have been celebrating a creative milestone after completing the Arts Award Discover, a nationally recognised qualification from Trinity College London.
The project, aimed at Year 1 and Year 2 pupils, introduced children to a wide range of artistic experiences, from painting and sculpture to photography and performance. Over the course of the year, students created personal ‘arts logs’ to document their journey, which included hands-on workshops, artist research, and collaborative projects.
The school community played a vital role in the project’s success. Parents volunteered their time and talents in a series of showcase assemblies, inspiring children with real-life stories from careers in the arts. Visitors included a ballet dancer, a makeup artist, a photographer, a violinist, a DJ, and an illustrator currently exhibiting in Paris.
One of the highlights was an open-air art workshop on the village green, where children created layered artworks using acrylics, Indian ink, and pastels. These pieces were later framed and displayed in a school gallery, alongside collaborative navy-and-gold paintings and mod-roc sculptures inspired by a visit to Watts Gallery and the work of local artist Mary Watts.
Headteacher Marion Stevens praised the project’s impact:
“The wealth of experiences the children received by taking part in this project have been incredible. They’ve been inspired by people’s careers—things they had never even thought of. They’ve also learned how the skills they’re developing now can be used in artistic careers in the future.”
Each child who completed the programme received an official certificate from Trinity College London, recognising their creativity and commitment.
Due to its success, St John’s plans to run the Arts Award Discover project every two years, continuing to nurture creativity and confidence in its youngest learners.

Our Governors
Together we oversee, challenge, support and act as a critical friend to the Headteacher and her team, as we plan the future direction and strategic vision of the school, that will best serve the interests of our current and future children. We do this by:
The Full Governing Body meets once a term. If you would like to attend a meeting please contact the Clerk to the Governors, Verina Gibson on vgibson@stjohns-farnham.surrey.sch.uk.
Governors also serve on Committees and in working groups, which meet once or twice a term to help deliver the work streams needed.
Individual governors have responsibility for Child Protection, Safeguarding, Special Educational Needs, Resources, Health and Safety and links with the Diocese and Babcock training provider.
At St John’s our governors are nominated by the Diocese of Guildford, the local PCC, teaching staff and parents. They serve a term of four years, although they can continue for subsequent terms. It is a voluntary role and we endeavour to recruit volunteers with skills that will enable the school to achieve its priority targets.
As St John’s is a voluntary aided school at least half of the governors must be Foundation Governors. Foundation Governors are representative of the Church of England, and are the school’s link with parishes, deaneries and the diocese.
Parent Governors bring the views of parents to the Governing Body, but they speak and act as individuals. They do not vote for all parents in general. They have equal status in the work of the Governing Body and have voting rights. We are currently looking for one more parent governor so if you are interested, please contact the school office.
Click here to see the Governor's Register of Interest & Attendance Register
For further information on strategy and finance do take a look at our dedicated page.
I joined the governing body in 2017 - both my children attended St John’s and it gave them the very best start to their learning journey. I am a Surrey Local Leader in Governance and a Trustee of a South West London MAT. My background is in ICT, and with over 20 years' experience within both public and private sectors, I now run my own marketing consultancy company. I passionately believe that schools have a responsibility to provide the best academic education and a caring, safe and most of all, happy and enjoyable environment where children are treated as unique individuals and supported to achieve their full potential. Working with our governing body, our partners and our wider community, I aim to create that unique and nurturing environment for the children at St John's.
I am delighted to be a governor and enjoy learning from and working with my committed and enthusiastic fellow governors and all the staff at the school. I am founder of my own company which I set up over 16 years ago, and the best part of my work involves mentoring and guiding young students who find education a struggle. I strongly believe that formative educational experiences are the key to successful career outcomes and I relish the opportunity to be part of a school that has such a warm and caring environment for all. My main focus as a governor is to ensure we are all mindful of mental health and wellbeing, alongside maintaining the very high academic standards achieved at the school, particularly in a rapidly changing world.
I jumped at the chance to become a governor for St John's and was thrilled to be appointed. Although I have only lived here since 2021, my family and I have been living in this beautiful area for almost twenty years. I was keenly involved in the PTA at my children’s school as I have always been interested in education, inspired both by my mum who worked as a teacher when I was growing up and as a lecturer myself. By trade I am a historian, information architect in IT, project manager and most recently a full time carer. I am keen to help support the school in their aspiration to see all children reach their full potential and I am looking forward to exploring what additional opportunities, resources and funding can be sourced to achieve this goal.
As the Vicar at St John’s, I am absolutely delighted to be an ex officio Governor. I have three grown up children and over the years have served on two other governing bodies of primary schools; although every school is different, as every child is different. The part time nature of my role may restrict the time I can offer, but I am committed to building great relationships between the school and the church, ensuring the centrality of the Christian faith within the school and being part of giving the children the best possible foundation for flourishing so that their lights can shine.
A resident of Churt for almost 40 years, I worked in business process, systems and information management roles for ICL, Xerox and, more recently, for Imperial College. Now retired, I am delighted to have more time to enjoy the outstanding natural environment that surrounds Churt, and for voluntary roles with 1st Churt Scout Group and local schools, in both the state and independent sectors. As a foundation governor at St John's, my special interests are to support the school in fostering creativity, valuing diversity, and in developing the children's understanding of the natural sciences, and an appreciation of the natural environment.
I have lived in Churt for over 50 years. I became the Caretaker and Crossing Patrol Officer at St John’s School, where I spent a happy 25 years. As a former pupil of Tiffin Boys School, Kingston, I am very keen to help maintain the highest possible standard of learning at St John’s within a happy and healthy environment. Wishing to continue my connection with the school I accepted a role on the Governing Body.
Lisa has had three children travel through St Johns, and loved it so much she never left, becoming a staff member in 2007. Since then she has supported countless children and staff. Lisa has a passion for developing confident readers in English. She also works hard to ensure children have the necessary skills in maths to understand the number system. Lisa relished the opportunity to support St Johns further by becoming a staff governor in September 2023.
My two children attended St Johns and I was instantly won over by its warmth. I am really proud to be working with this governing team delivering projects as part of the Full Governing Body. As a resident of Churt I am passionate about the school's connection with the community and local church. My day job is in communications so I hope to share my knowledge and experience in this area with the school. I look forward to supporting this unique and gorgeous village school, helping the pupils experience the best of infant school life.
Marion has been with the St John's family for over 19 years having worked across all year groups before undertaking the role of Head in December 2018. Marion is an inspirational and inclusive leader, with strong links within the community. Her drive for innovation combined with her sense of fun ensure all children thrive under her care.
I’m absolutely delighted to have been appointed as a parent governor for St John’s and to represent the parent community in school matters. With my youngest just beginning his St John’s journey and my eldest having recently completed his, I’m truly excited to help shape the future of the school and contribute to the educational experience of all its pupils.
St John’s is a wonderful place for children to learn and thrive—a caring, supportive and, above all, happy environment.
Professionally, I am a Town Planner and help run a private consultancy firm, advising a wide range of stakeholders across the planning spectrum. This work has taught me how to balance competing interests and reach practical, well-considered solutions—skills I look forward to bringing to my role as parent governor and to school life as a whole.
